title: Advance Commitment Credit Exceptions & Marketplace Offset Routing Playbook
creator: Aisha Carter
description:
Purpose:
This playbook defines a reproducible intake and routing process for customer requests related to: advance commitment credits, invoice adjustments for reserved capacity, marketplace revenue-offset requests, and cost-allocation exceptions. The goal is to reduce time-to-resolution for enterprise billing requests while ensuring correct revenue recognition and limiting manual finance work.

Scope (what this covers):
- Advance credit grants or exceptions for long-term commitments (commitments, pre-paid credits).
- Invoice re-issuance and partial refunds tied to commitments or marketplace offsets.
- Cost allocation corrections where billing tags were applied incorrectly (marketplace partner, internal cost center).
- One-off marketplace fee offsets (e.g., partner discount applied late).

Out of scope:
- Standard refund/backout process for simple usage disputes (handled by Finance Ops runbook).
- Bugs in billing engine; those should be routed to ENG backlog with a billing-incident tag.

Intake form (required fields to surface up-front):
- Request type (Advance Credit | Invoice Reissue | Marketplace Offset | Allocation Correction)
- Customer name & account ID
- Commitment ID or contract reference (if applicable)
- Total dollar impact and whether this is recurring or one-time
- Invoice numbers affected (if invoice-level change)
- Requested outcome (credit, reissue, offset, allocation change)
- Business justification (one-paragraph)
- Legal/contract flag (Yes/No) + link to contract doc (Drive/Confluence)
- Attach evidence (billing CSV, usage query, marketplace settlement)
- SLA requirement (business-critical date)

Prioritization heuristic (decision factors):
1) Revenue Risk: amount at stake and recognition impact.
2) Customer Tier: enterprise / dedicated customers get expedited routing.
3) Compliance/Legal Trigger: contract language that mandates action or regulatorily required corrections.
4) Operational Cost: manual work hours required from Finance/Engineering.
5) Downstream Impact: affects downstream metrics (MRR, Marketplace settlement windows).

Priority mapping (automated):
- P0: > $250k revenue impact OR regulatory/legal flag -> Escalate to Head of Finance + Legal (48h SLA for decision).
- P1: $25k–$250k OR enterprise customer SLAs -> PM + Finance validation (5 business days).
- P2: <$25k and no contractual/legal requirement -> Finance Ops triage (10 business days).

Routing & Approval flow (high level):
1) Intake form submission -> triage queue (Billing-Triage Slack channel).
2) Auto-classifier evaluates: request type, estimated dollars, presence of contract link.
3) PM on duty (rotating) validates completeness within 24–48h.
4) Finance verifies invoicing data & impacts; for marketplace offsets, Partner Ops confirms partner settlement window.
5) If legal/contract required or >$50k, Legal review requested concurrently.
6) Decision track: Approve credit | Request more info | Escalate to exec sign-off.
7) If engineering change required (billing engine or allocation mapping), create ENG ticket with billable scope, attach proof, and mark dependency.
8) Once approved, Finance Ops executes the invoice adjustment/credit and records journal entry.

SLA targets:
- Triage acknowledgement: <= 24 hours for enterprise; <= 48 hours for others.
- Decision window: P0: 48 hours; P1: 5 business days; P2: 10 business days.
- Execution (Finance post-decision): <= 3 business days for credit/invoice adjustments.

Automation & tooling suggestions:
- Intake form hosted in Zendesk/Confluence form with fields above + auto-ticket creation in Linear with label pm-billing-intake.
- Classifier webhook that tags severity based on dollar threshold and contract flag.
- A Slack workflow to post new high-priority items to #billing-escalations with direct links to the Linear ticket and required artifacts.
- Dashboard (Looker/Grafana) tile to show open billing exceptions by aging and dollar impact.

Data required for decisions:
- Usage reports for affected windows (CSV), generated via internal billing queries.
- Original invoice PDF and invoice metadata (date, sequence, recipient).
- Contract or SOW clause that justifies the exception if claimed.
- Marketplace settlement report from Partner Ops showing partner fees and timing.

Acceptance criteria (what "done" looks like):
- A documented decision and owner assigned in Linear, including the executed accounting journal reference.
- If engineering work required, ENG ticket created with acceptance criteria and linked PR in GH.
- Customer notified with templated message and changes reflected on next invoice/adjustment.
- Postmortem if decision was escalated to execs or if manual effort > 8 hours.

Examples (common scenarios and routing):
- Scenario A: Enterprise customer prepaid commitment misapplied to another account -> P1 -> PM + Finance validate -> credit issued; ENG creates allocation fix.
- Scenario B: Marketplace partner requests offset due to late fee reversal -> P2 if <$25k and within same settlement window -> Partner Ops + Finance handle.
- Scenario C: Contract clause explicitly requires early credit on termination -> P0 -> Legal + Finance + PM triage and expedite.

Training & rollout plan:
- Week 0: Publish this playbook in Confluence + a short internal explainer (500 words).
- Week 1: Live 2x30m training sessions for Sales AMs, Finance Ops, Partner Ops.
- Week 2–6: Pilot with top 10 enterprise accounts; collect metrics (time-to-resolution, dollars processed, number of escalations).
- Week 7: Iterate and publish v1.1 with templates and Slack automations.

Metrics to track (dashboard):
- Mean time to decision (by priority bucket).
- Dollars adjusted per week and per customer.
- % of requests requiring engineering changes.
- Reopened disputes after adjustment (quality gate).

Links & artifacts:
acceptance_criteria: Intake form with required fields is published and creates Linear tickets automatically.
Routing classifier applies correct priority tag in >= 90% of sampled cases.
SLA acknowledgement and decision windows met for >= 80% of pilot requests.
Finance journal entries recorded and linked in Linear ticket for every executed adjustment.
